# CLAUDE.md

## core-testing

# Core testing

- Run the focused test for the file you changed before declaring done.
- Add a test for any new behaviour; prefer a few focused cases over coverage.
- Write the test for a piece of code immediately after (or while) writing the
  code, not in a batch at the end. For a large piece, write its tests as you go,
  section by section. A change is not done until its tests exist and pass.
- Never delete or weaken an existing test to make a build pass.
- Test runs must emit a machine-readable coverage report (e.g. pytest
  `--cov-report=json:coverage.json`, jest `--coverage`), configured in the
  project's test config so a plain test run always produces it. The GUI
  reads the report and shows per-part coverage; a test run without a
  coverage report leaves the map blank.

## quality-checks

# Quality checks

- Never bypass, suppress, or weaken a quality check (pre-commit hook, linter, type checker, test) without explicit user approval.
- Prohibited without approval: `git commit --no-verify`, `SKIP=<hook>`, `# noqa`, `# type: ignore`, `// @ts-ignore`, `eslint-disable`, `@pytest.mark.skip`, loosening thresholds in config files.
- When a check fails, fix the code first. If an override is genuinely necessary, present the issue, the alternatives considered, and ask for approval before proceeding.
- "The check is annoying", "it's faster to skip", and "the code works fine" are not valid reasons.
- Never delete or weaken an existing test to make a build pass.

## state-hygiene

# State hygiene

The viewer is only as trustworthy as `.claude-gui/state.yaml`. Keep it honest.

## Decompose todos into sub-tasks

- A todo that bundles more than one deliverable (a phase with several files,
  a feature with build + test + docs) MUST be split into `children` sub-todos,
  one per deliverable. A single bullet that hides a lot of work is a bug.
- Give each sub-todo its own `id`, `text`, `status`, `owner`, and `node`
  (pointing at the structure part it belongs to).
- A parent with no status of its own is derived from its children: done when
  all are done, in_progress when any is, blocked when any is blocked.
- Keep the tree shallow: one level of sub-todos is enough; split a sub-todo
  further only if it itself hides multiple deliverables.

## Refresh the stamp at every phase boundary

- Update `todos` (statuses) AND the top-level `updated` field together, every
  time a phase or deliverable changes state. Never update one without the other.
- `updated` is the freshness gate: `setup/doctor.py` fails if the last
  `events.jsonl` entry is newer than `updated` by more than 15 minutes. A
  stale stamp is a broken install, not a cosmetic issue.
- When you finish work, the last thing you do is bring `state.yaml` current:
  flip the todos, bump `updated`, and re-run `setup/doctor.py` to confirm it
  exits 0.

## stack-base-coding-practices

# Coding practices

- Solve the problem with the least code and complexity that works. No premature optimization, no speculative features.
- Prefer standard library and widely-accepted patterns. Introduce a third-party dependency only when it is the industry standard for the task.
- Make the minimum change required. Do not refactor, reformat, or "clean up" code that the task does not touch.
- Integrate new logic into the existing structure rather than replacing working blocks.
- Verify facts that could be version-dependent (APIs, library behavior, config syntax) with tools or docs instead of relying on memory.
- Explain the *why* behind non-obvious decisions in one or two sentences.
